convert an IN subquery to a semi-join

FROM store_sales
WHERE ss_store_sk IN (SELECT s_store_sk FROM store WHERE s_store_name = 'ese')
  AND ss_sold_time_sk IN (SELECT t_time_sk FROM time_dim WHERE t_hour = 8 AND t_minute >= 30)
  AND ss_hdemo_sk IN (SELECT hd_demo_sk FROM household_demographics WHERE hd_dep_count = 0)

1. COVERING COMPOSITE INDEX — TARGET: `store_sales(ss_store_sk, ss_sold_time_sk, ss_hdemo_sk)` — TRANSFORMATION: create a B-tree index on these three fact-table FK columns so all three dimension predicates can be resolved inside an index scan and `count(*)` can be answered as an index-only count, eliminating the full 57.6M-row heap scan; refresh statistics afterward.

2. SEMI-JOIN FILTER (store) — TARGET: `store_sales.ss_store_sk` joined from `store.s_store_name = 'ese'` — TRANSFORMATION: rewrite the `store` join as a semi-join against the small set of `s_store_sk` values whose store name is `'ese'`, so only matching store key(s) are used to probe the new index.

3. SEMI-JOIN FILTER (time-of-day) — TARGET: `store_sales.ss_sold_time_sk` joined from `time_dim.t_hour = 8 AND t_minute >= 30` — TRANSFORMATION: rewrite the `time_dim` join as a semi-join against the `t_time_sk` values in the 8:30–8:59 window, pushing this highly selective time restriction directly onto `store_sales`.

4. SEMI-JOIN FILTER (household) — TARGET: `store_sales.ss_hdemo_sk` joined from `household_demographics.hd_dep_count = 0` — TRANSFORMATION: rewrite the `household_demographics` join as a semi-join against the matching `hd_demo_sk` values, applying the remaining household selectivity after store and time have already narrowed the scanned index range.

5. REMOVE NO-OP ORDER/LIMIT — TARGET: final `ORDER BY count(*) LIMIT 100` — TRANSFORMATION: drop both clauses because an ungrouped `count(*)` always returns exactly one row, so ordering and limiting cannot affect the result.
